contexts.text: They who are being led and taught are called the flock... But they who are not being led to good, and who are not learning good, are not the flock. Illustrated.
They who lead the flock to the good of charity, are they who gather the flock; but they who do not lead to the good of charity, are they who scatter it.
The firstlings of the flock () = that which is of the Lord alone.
The shepherd of the flock = the good of charity; but here shepherd is not mentioned, but father;neither is flock mentioned, but cattle.
(Abram) had flock and herd... () = all things in general which pertain to scientifics... The flock and herd = the possessions.
Cattle and flock = good.
(Lot) had flock and herd and tents () = the things with which the external man abounds; (thus) the possessions of the external man... Flock, herd, and tents, here, = those things which cannot agree.

The reason flock and herd = the possessions of the external man, may be evident from the signification of flock and herd, which is goods; but here, the things which are to be separated, thus non-goods. Illustrated.
The sacrifices from the herd = celestial natural things, and those from the flock, celestial rational things.
Milk of the flock () = the Celestial Spiritual of the Rational.

(Abimelech took) flock and herd () = that (the doctrine of faith) was enriched with rational goods and natural goods. Those within the Church who are truly rational, that is, who are internal men, are called the flock; hence it is that by a flock is also signified in the abstract rational or internal goods themselves. But those within the Church are called the herd who are natural, that is, external men; and hence by a herd is also signified in the abstract, natural or external goods themselves. References.
The flock of which he will take the tenth () = the remains of good to which he will do violence.
Abraham took flock and herd, and gave to Abimelech () = Divine goods implanted in the rational things of doctrine.
The flock of Kedar () = Divine celestial things.
(Jehovah) hath given him flock and herd () = goods in general.
The flock of Kedar = spiritual good. a flock = spiritual good. References.
Tents and flocks () = the goods the Spiritual Church... It is the holy things of worship which are signified by tents and flocks...
(Isaac) had possession of flock and possession of herd () = as to interior good and as to exterior good, that is, as to rational good and as to natural good.

Go I pray to the flock () = domestic natural good, not conjoined with the Divine Rational. Flock = good, here, natural good, because Jacob is addressed, in fact domestic good, because it was at home... Otherwise, flock, in the Word, is predicated of the good of the Rational, but then herd is predicated of the good of the Natural.
Flocks = the goods of charity. References.

Three droves of a flock lying near it () = the holy things of the Church and of doctrinal things... Specifically, a flock = those who are within the Church, and who learn and imbue the goods of charity and the truths of faith... But, in general, a flock = all those who are in good, thus those who belong to the Lord's Church in the whole earth; and as all these are introduced into good and truth by means of doctrinal things, a flock also = doctrinal things. Explained.
They watered the flock () = doctrine... For a flock = those who are in the goods and truths of faith.
(Rachel) cometh with the flock () = interior doctrinal things. A flock = the Church, and also doctrinal things; here, interior doctrinal things, because predicated of Rachel... AC 3793. AC 3797.
The fructification and multiplication of truth and good is signified by the flock which Jacob acquired by means of the flock of Laban. AC 3971:2. AC 3987.
This (collateral) good is signified by the flock of Laban, by means of which Jacob acquired his flock. AC 3982:2.

I will return, I will feed, I will keep thy flock () = that the good represented by Laban was to be applied to use, namely, to that of introducing genuine goods and truths; for the flock, here that of Laban, = the good represented by him.
I will pass through all thy flock today () = that he perceives every good as to its quality; flock = good.

It now treats of this fructification of good and the multiplication of truth... signified by the flock which Jacob acquired by means of the flock of Laban. Flock, here, = good and truth, as is frequently the case in the Word; the flock of Laban, the good which is represented by Laban... the flock of Jacob, genuine good and truth, which is procured by means of the former.
A flock, in the Word, = good and truth, or, what is the same, those who are in good and truth, thus who belong to the Lord's Church.
Jacob fed the rest of Laban's flocks () = that from those which were left he took those goods and truths which were to be conjoined. Flocks = goods and truths.
Over against the flocks () = that truths and goods might be conjoined with the Natural.
And the flocks grew warm at the rods () = the effect of affection from their Own power. AC 4029.
(Jacob) had many flocks () = the interior goods and truths thence derived.

To send to them and call the field to his flock () = to adjoin to himself; field = ... where good is; and the flock, the goods and truths themselves which are now acquired, to which the affections of truth meant by Rachel and Leah were applied...
Laban had gone to shear his flock () = the state of use and the end of the good signified by the flock of Laban.
Six years in thy flock () = that afterwards he might acquire good.
The flock is my flock () = that all... the goods were his.
Flock () = interior natural good.
Flock () = interior goods, and also non-goods.
The flocks and herds giving suck with me () = interior goods and natural goods which have not as yet acquired Divine life.
Their flocks and their herds () = that they destroyed rational good and natural good.
And the peace of the flock () = how the case was with those who were learning, that is, the Church.
He went up to the shearers of his flock () = somewhat of elevation to consult for the Church.
Flocks and oxen () = goods internal and external.
Flock () = those who are being instructed.

And thy flocks, and thy herds () = natural good interior and exterior... The reason herd = exterior good, and flocks interior, is that the beasts which constituted a herd, as oxen and bullocks, in the sacrifices signified the external goods of charity, and also the goods of the external man; whereas those which constituted the flocks, as lambs, sheep, goats, signified the internal goods of charity, and also the goods of the internal man; and therefore they who are in these latter goods are called in the Word a flock, and he who leads them a shepherd. AC 6044. AC 6046. AC 8937. Explained.

That they correspond is evident from the fact that when from heavenly affection the Angels are talking together about the goods of charity, there appear... flocks and herds; flocks when they are talking about the interior goods of charity, and herds when about the exterior ones.
Their flocks and their herds () = the interior and the exterior goods of truth. Explained.
For the cattle of the flock, and for the cattle of the herd () = the interior and the exterior goods of truth.
To hear the hissings of the flocks () = contempt from those who are in the good of charity.
And their flocks () = charity; (for) flocks = the interior good of charity.
To water the flocks = to instruct from the Word in good.
A flock = those who learn and who are led to the good of charity. References.
(Moses) watered their flock () = that those who were in good were instructed thence... A flock = those who learn and are led to the good of charity; thus those who are in good.

He watered the flock () = those who are of the Church there. A flock = those who are in good and who suffer themselves to be instructed; here, those who were of the Church there... A flock = both good and the Church, that is, those who are in good and those who are of the Church, for these things are so joined together that the one cannot be separated from the other...
Moses was feeding the flock of Jethro... () = that the law from the Divine was instructing those who were in the truth of simple good.

A flock = one who learns and is led by means of truth to the good of charity; thus in the general sense a flock = the Church, here the Church where were those who were in the truth of simple good. AC 6828.
Upon the herd and upon the flock () = the voluntary things; the herd = the good of the exterior Natural; and the flock = the good of the interior Natural; thus they = what is voluntary.
With our flock and with our herd will we go () = those who are in interior good and in exterior good.
Only your flock and your herd shall stay () = that they shall not worship the Lord from good; a flock = interior good, and a herd exterior good.
Also take your flocks and your herds () = the interior and the exterior goods of charity.
Flock and herd, very much acquisition () = the good acquired by means of truth, interior and exterior, in great abundance.
Thy flocks and thy herds () = goods internal and external. Explained.
(The animals of the flock and of the herd respectively, enumerated.) AC 9391.
See Cattle, pecudis.
Flock = interior good.
The beasts of the flock = affections of internal truth and good; and the beasts of the herd, affections of external truth and good. AC 9391.
The flocks of Arabia () = all the goods of the external man... Flocks = the goods of the internal man; and Arabia, where the good is.
See Cattle or Cattle.

Also the flock and the herd shall not feed over against this mountain () = that neither could they be instructed concerning the interior and the exterior good of the Church, of worship, and of the Word.
That flock and herd = the interior and the exterior good with man. Illustrated.
There appeared in the Spiritual World two flocks, one of goats and the other of sheep... TCR 506.
The Angel divided the sheep into two flocks...
Ministers of God, seduce not the flock. (Then) the greater part of the flock on the left hand... joined the flock on the right.
The animals of the herd = the affections of good and truth in the external or natural man; and those of the flock, the affections of good and truth in the internal or spiritual man. Enumerated.
The flock of man with which the waste cities shall be full () = spiritual truths with which the doctrine of the Church will be full.
The flock which He shall feed as a shepherd () = those who are in the good of charity.
Flocks = interior goods and truths, which are called spiritual. References.
Sons of the flock = spiritual truths; and sons of the herd, natural truths.
Which shall eat up thy flock and thy herd () = truths and goods internal and external.
Flocks = interior goods and truths... which are spiritual; herds, exterior goods and truths, which are natural. Enumerated. AE 513:9. AE 650:6, Enumerated. AE 724:27. AE 911:14. AE 1100:4.
The flock of thine heritage () = those of the Church who are in the spiritual things of the Word, which are the truths of its internal sense.
Flock () = spiritual truth.
The shepherd and his flock () = those who teach and those who learn.
